dataset.disclaimer: NLEM membership, healthcare level (P = primary, S = secondary, T = tertiary), dosage forms and strengths come from the official NLEM 2022 gazette notification. Class and mechanism notes are study material and are blank where they have not been added; the NLEM document does not contain them. Always check against a pharmacology reference before relying on them. Not a prescribing guide.

A beta-lactam antibiotic that binds penicillin-binding proteins and interferes with bacterial cell-wall synthesis.
Amoxicillin interferes with bacterial cell-wall synthesis; clavulanic acid inhibits some beta-lactamase enzymes.
Binds penicillin-binding proteins and interferes with bacterial cell-wall synthesis.
Binds the bacterial 50S ribosomal subunit and interferes with protein synthesis.

listings.category: Medicines used in the Management of HIV

medicines.mechanismOfAction: Binds the bacterial 30S ribosomal subunit and interferes with protein synthesis.
In susceptible anaerobes and protozoa, reactive metabolites damage DNA and disrupt nucleic-acid function.
Inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV, disrupting DNA replication.
Inhibits bacterial DNA-dependent RNA polymerase, disrupting RNA synthesis.
After activation in susceptible bacteria, inhibits mycolic-acid synthesis, an important part of the mycobacterial cell wall.
Lowers hepatic glucose production and improves insulin sensitivity; its cellular effects are complex.

listings.sectionTitle: Hormones, other Endocrine Medicines and Contraceptives

medicines.mechanismOfAction: Activates insulin receptors, promoting glucose uptake in some tissues and reducing hepatic glucose output.

listings.sectionTitle: Hormones, other Endocrine Medicines and Contraceptives

medicines.mechanismOfAction: Closes ATP-sensitive potassium channels in pancreatic beta cells, stimulating insulin release.
Blocks L-type calcium channels, especially in vascular smooth muscle, promoting vasodilation.
Reduces angiotensin-converting enzyme activity, lowering formation of angiotensin II.
Blocks angiotensin II type 1 receptors, reducing signalling through that receptor.
Inhibits the sodium-chloride cotransporter in the distal convoluted tubule of the kidney.
Inhibits the sodium-potassium-chloride cotransporter in the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle.
Inhibits HMG-CoA reductase, an enzyme involved in cholesterol synthesis.
Inhibits the gastric parietal-cell hydrogen-potassium ATPase, reducing acid secretion.
Blocks serotonin 5-HT3 receptors involved in nausea and vomiting pathways.

An artemisinin derivative; activation in malaria parasites produces reactive species that damage parasite components.
Artemether acts rapidly against parasites; lumefantrine has a complementary antimalarial effect, including interference with parasite heme handling.
